A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Diptera are a highly effective group of insects for biodiversity studies in rain forest.

, for Diptera, a combination of yellow pan (water), canopy knockdown and Malaise traps is the best method for sampling the fauna of these sites and that the family level analyses provide the most useful insights into patterns in the assemblages.
, in the case of Diptera, the family level is a useful level at which to analyse biodiversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, at the family level, there are clear patterns in dipteran diversity across sites, and these patterns reflect the biogeography of the sites, and the floristic composition.
the Diptera are an excellent taxon for use in comparative biodiversity analyses.
